:::{#sol-prereq-trace-recursion}

1. `p(3, 4)` returns 81.
   The calls are
   `p(3, 4) = 3 * p(3, 3)`,
   `p(3, 3) = 3 * p(3, 2)`,
   `p(3, 2) = 3 * p(3, 1)`,
   `p(3, 1) = 3 * p(3, 0)`
   and `p(3, 0) = 1`,
   so `p(3, 4)` is $3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 81$.
2. Five calls: one for each of `n` = 4, 3, 2, 1 and 0.
3. `p(b, n)` computes $b^n$, the `n`th power of `b`.

The course writes many functions like this one, in Racket rather than Python,
starting in [Functional Programming](functional-programming.qmd)
and continuing in [Recursion](recursion.qmd).
If tracing it was hard, review recursion from CSCI 145 before the course reaches it.

:::
